supplemental_signals.covenant_compliance: In compliance both 10-K (Mar 2024) and Q3 10-Q (Dec 2024); revolver paid to $0
supplemental_signals.insider_pattern: CEO sold ~1,000 shares Sept 16 2024 at $336-$345 (post-offering, above raise price); CFO 10b5-1 adopted Nov 4 2024; CSO/EVP sold ~1,500 shares May 15 2025. All small relative to total comp; tax-driven post-vest pattern dominant.
supplemental_signals.acquisition_cadence: 7 acquisitions since TRUaire (Dec 2020); FY24 1 deal $34.7M; FY25 YTD-Q3 2 deals $90M cumulative — pace not aggressive vs $164M OCF/yr
supplemental_signals.drawdown_context: Pre-cutoff drawdown -24.1% with no financial-distress signals in filings; organic revenue decelerating to +1.9% in most recent quarter; gross margin compressing on freight. Most likely explanation is multiple compression on a richly valued (~$285 equity raise) compounder with softening organic growth.

summary: CSW Industrials presents as a healthy diversified industrial: no going-concern language, clean Grant Thornton 10-year tenure, fully covenant-compliant, customer base diversified (no >10% concentration), FCF margin ~18%, dividend raised twice in two years, buyback authorization doubled. The -24.1% drawdown is NOT corroborated by distress signals in the filings. Two Mode-B concerns mitigate (not invalidate) the LONG read: (1) organic revenue growth decelerated to +1.9% in the most recent disclosed quarter (Q3 FY25) with M&A increasingly carrying the headline; gross margin slipped on freight; (2) management opportunistically raised $360M of equity at $285 in Sept 2024 and CEO sold ~$340K of stock 12 days later — capital-structure-optimization behavior, not distress. Verdict: LONG-tier (boring-middle, honestly disclosed cyclical softness within an otherwise healthy compounder; the framework's job here is to NOT flag this name).
